extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of public relations (PR) and PR educators
extracted.subtask_description: Chapter excerpt introducing contemporary public relations: definitions, core functions, distinctions from related fields (marketing, advertising), and the major specialties (internal relations, publicity, advertising, press agentry, public affairs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Harlow compiled definition of public relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Public relations is the distinctive management function which helps establish and maintain mutual lines of communication, understanding, acceptance and cooperation between an organization and its publics; involves the management of problems or issues; helps management to keep informed on and responsive to public opinion; defines and emphasizes the responsibility of management to serve the public interest; helps management keep abreast of and effectively utilize change, serving as an early warning system to help anticipate trends; and uses research and sound and ethical communication as its principal tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This long-form definition enumerates roles PR must fulfill (communication, issue management, counseling management, serving public interest, trend anticipation) and prescribes research and ethical communication as principal tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA short definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Public relations is a strategic communication process that builds mutually beneficial relationships between organizations and their publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes PR as strategic, relationship-focused, and mutually beneficial rather than merely publicity or advertising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipating, analyzing, and interpreting public opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipating, analyzing, and interpreting public opinion, attitudes, and issues that might impact, for good or ill, the operations and plans of the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A core management task: monitor external and internal opinion and issues to forecast impacts on organizational goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counseling management on public ramifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Counseling management at all levels in the organization with regard to policy decisions, courses of action, and communication, taking into account their public ramifications and the organization’s social or citizenship responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR acts as a counselor to management, recommending policies and actions that balance organizational aims with public acceptability and social responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researching, conducting, and evaluating programs of action and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Researching, conducting, and evaluating, on a continuing basis, programs of action and communication to achieve the informed public understanding necessary to the success of an organization’s aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs may include marketing, financial, fundraising, employee, community or government relations; continuous evaluation and research are expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning and implementing efforts to influence public policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning and implementing the organization’s efforts to influence or change public policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes public affairs, lobbying-related activities, community engagement and policy-oriented communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing PR resources (objectives, planning, budgeting, staffing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting objectives, planning, budgeting, recruiting and training staff, developing facilities—in short, managing the resources needed to perform all of the above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR is a management function that must set measurable objectives and allocate resources (staff, budget, facilities) to meet them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge and disciplines required for PR practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of the knowledge that may be required in the professional practice of public relations include communication arts, psychology, social psychology, sociology, political science, economics, and the principles of management and ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical skills (opinion research, media relations, direct mail, institutional advertising, publications, film/video, events, speeches) are also required depending on role.

rubrics_metrics.name: PR uses professional communication skills as an integrative role
rubrics_metrics.description: In helping to define and implement policy, the public relations practitioner uses a variety of professional communication skills and plays an integrative role both within the organization and between the organization and the external environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR practitioners coordinate across departments (HR, legal, marketing) and with external publics to ensure consistent, strategic messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conducts a planned and sustained program by management
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducts a planned and sustained program by an organization’s management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR is ongoing and strategic, not ad hoc publicity; requires planning and management oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deals with relationships between organization and stakeholder publics
rubrics_metrics.description: Deals with the relationships between an organization and its stakeholder publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus is on mutually interdependent parties (employees, customers, communities, shareholders) whose attitudes affect organizational success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitors awareness, opinions, attitudes, and behaviors
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitors awareness, opinions, attitudes, and behaviors inside and outside the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement and monitoring are required to detect shifts and inform strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyzes impact of policies/procedures on publics
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyzes the impact of policies, procedures, and actions on stakeholder publics to identify those that conflict with the public interest and organizational survival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR should flag policies that risk damaging relationships or reputation and recommend adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counsels management to establish mutually beneficial policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Counsels management to establish new policies, procedures, and actions that benefit both the organization and its publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory role aimed at aligning organizational objectives with public expectations and societal norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishes and maintains two-way communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishes and maintains two-way communication between the organization and its publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes dialogue and listening (not only one-way broadcasting) as central to effective PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produces measurable changes in awareness, opinion, attitude, and behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Produces measurable changes in awareness, opinion, attitude, and behavior inside and outside the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR outcomes should be measurable; effectiveness judged by observable shifts in target publics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results in new and/or maintained relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Results in new and/or maintained relationships between an organization and its publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ultimate aim: create or sustain relationships that support organizational survival and goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicity (newsworthiness and uncontrolled media placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicity is information provided by an outside source that is used by media because the information has news value. This is an uncontrolled method of placing messages in the media because the source does not pay for placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To generate publicity practitioners must know what will attract media attention, identify a newsworthy angle and lead, and write and package content appropriately for each medium; trust from journalists helps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successful publicity events characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful publicity events have real news value; appeal to media gatekeepers; offer photo, video, or sound opportunities; and communicate the source’s intended message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design events (groundbreakings, dedications, press conferences) to be newsworthy and media-friendly to maximize coverage and message control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising as controlled media placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertising is information placed in the media by an identified sponsor that pays for the time or space. It is a controlled method of placing messages in the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertising gives sponsors control over content, placement, and timing; in PR it is used for nonmarketing purposes (reputation management, public education, addressing criticism) when budget allows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press agentry — creating newsworthy stories to attract attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Press agentry is creating newsworthy stories and events to attract media attention in order to gain public notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press agentry emphasizes publicity over understanding; tactics may aim to create perception of newsworthiness and sometimes use sensational or deceptive means; useful in entertainment, celebrity, and event-driven industries but differs from relationship-focused PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal relations / employee communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal relations is the specialized part of public relations that builds and maintains a mutually beneficial relationship between managers and the employees on whom an organization’s success depends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal relations staff plan and implement programs to keep employees informed and motivated, coordinate with HR and legal, and align internal and external messaging so the organization 'speaks with one voice.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Public affairs — PR for influencing public policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Public affairs is the specialized part of public relations that builds and maintains organizational relationships with governmental agencies and community stakeholder groups to influence public policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public affairs roles include government relations, community relations, lobbying-style activities; practitioners should navigate regulatory processes honestly and transparently. Typical responsibilities: federal/state/local government affairs, community relations, PACs/contributions, grassroots support, and issues management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of honest and transparent communications in public affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Particularly in public affairs, relationships are done through honest and transparent communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical transparency is emphasized as essential for credibility when engaging with government and policy stakeholders.
